overall: The AG found the committee violated the Open Meeting Law by entering executive session on October 25, 2018 under the litigation purpose without a permissible basis, and ordered release of those minutes. Notice and procedure allegations about that meeting were untimely; posting-time and recurring-agenda allegations were not violations, though the generic executive session item was flagged as insufficient.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the committee regularly lists executive session on agendas even when none is planned, using a generic standing item.
allegations.key_passage: However, since the Committee never met in executive session at the March 12, 2019, meeting, we find no violation of the Open Meeting Law in that instance.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the October 25, 2018 notice lacked adequate executive session detail, citing the generic 'Executive Session Chapter 30A §21' item.
allegations.key_passage: Here, any deficiencies in the notice for the October 25, 2018, meeting or in the Chair’s open session statement of the purpose for executive session could have been discovered right away.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the committee entered executive session on October 25, 2018 without sufficiently stating the purpose in open session.
allegations.key_passage: Since the first complaint was not filed with the Committee until February 13, 2019, we find these two allegations to be untimely and therefore decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the October 25, 2018 executive session under the litigation purpose was improper because no permissible purpose existed.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by convening in executive session under Purpose 3 for this discussion.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the committee improperly refused to release minutes of the October 25, 2018 executive session; the letter orders their release.
allegations.key_passage: We also order the Committee to publicly release its October 25, 2018, executive session minutes within 30 days of the receipt of this determination.

allegations.summary: Complaint said the committee does not record the date and time notices were posted; the website shows a stamp beside each agenda.
allegations.key_passage: Here, since the Committee included date and time stamps on the website next to each agenda documenting when it was posted, we do not find a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Publicly release the October 25, 2018 executive session minutes within 30 days of receipt of the determination.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of a similar violation in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law.
